dek: A thin day: a Two Minute Papers video frames DeepMind's Gemini 4 Neon as a shift in the race, and Hugging Face puts video generation on Trainium3.
brief: Two Minute Papers argues in a new video that DeepMind's latest release has changed the AI race. The video's description points to a DeepMind security report on Gemini 4 Neon. The video comes from a single commentator, and no benchmark figures were in front of us, so the framing is a claim to watch rather than a ranking change.

Hugging Face published a post on generating videos with LTX-2.5 on Trainium3, an item for the hardware-diversity and efficiency storylines. Matthew Berman also posted a short on how Tesla generates its third-person view of the road.

top_stories.title: Two Minute Papers says DeepMind's new model changed the AI race, and points to a Gemini 4 Neon safety report
top_stories.summary: Two Minute Papers titles its new video "DeepMind's New AI Just Changed The AI Race." The description cites a DeepMind security report on Gemini 4 Neon and lists a long set of social posts as sources.
top_stories.why: The claim comes from a commentator rather than a measured result, but a DeepMind safety document for a new model is the kind of lab disclosure the misalignment thread tracks, and it deserves a direct read.

top_stories.title: Hugging Face takes LTX-2.5 video generation to Trainium3
top_stories.summary: Hugging Face's post, titled "Taking Trainium3 to the Track: Generating Videos with LTX-2.5," covers generating video with the LTX-2.5 model on Trainium3 hardware. The post text was not available to us beyond its title.
top_stories.why: Running a video model on non-Nvidia accelerators is a data point for how much of the serving stack can move off the default hardware, though without the post's numbers there is nothing to compare yet.

top_stories.title: Matthew Berman explains how Tesla generates its third-person reality view
top_stories.summary: Matthew Berman's short, "How Tesla Generates Its Third-Person Reality View," looks at how Tesla produces its third-person rendering of the world around the car. The description holds only promotional links, so we have no detail on his explanation.
top_stories.why: It is a reminder that deployed perception systems, not just chat models, are a large part of where applied AI is visible to ordinary users.
